title: Scanner page -- run a scan, review candidates, add hits to the watchlist
description: A new page, not a section of the watchlist or ticker detail view (per docs/ideas.md's own scoping): pick a scan category, run it, review the resulting candidate list, and add any worth tracking to the watchlist (POST /api/watchlist, already built) -- each hit's drill-down is the existing ticker detail view. Must clearly show a disabled/unavailable state (not an error) when IBKR isn't connected, consistent with the backend's own degrade-gracefully contract.

checklist.step: Build a new Scanner page: category picker, a 'run scan' action, and a results list with each hit linking to the ticker detail view (TickerLink) and an 'add to watchlist' action per row.
Show a clear, non-error disabled state when the backend reports IBKR unavailable/disabled.
Add the page to app navigation.
Component tests covering: available with results, available with zero results, and the disabled/unavailable state.

decisions.decision: New common/UnavailableState component (with its own Storybook stories + test) renders the 'the feature is disabled/not reachable right now, nothing is actually broken' case -- distinct from both common/ErrorState (genuine ApiError, red/alert styling, role="alert") and common/EmptyState (real data, just zero of it). ScannerPage renders it whenever GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's state !== 'available'; ScannerPanel renders it again for the same non-'available' outcome from POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run (reachable if IBKR drops between the params check and the run). This is the first frontend feature that needs to distinguish this three-way split (broken / disabled-but-fine / empty-but-fine) since this is the first UI built against any of the /api/ibkr/* routes.
decisions.rationale: Reusing EmptyState for the disabled state was rejected: this task's own checklist explicitly calls out 'available with zero results' and 'the disabled/unavailable state' as two scenarios a reviewer needs to be able to tell apart at a glance, and EmptyState's framing ('no data to show you') is a poor fit for 'this data source can't even be reached right now' -- conflating them under one component/message would blur exactly the distinction the checklist calls out. Reusing ErrorState (e.g. by synthesizing a fake ApiError for a 200 response) was also rejected: `disabled`/`gateway_unreachable`/`not_authenticated` are deliberately not ApiErrors at all (API.md, backend-market-scanner's own decisions) precisely so the frontend doesn't have to render them as failures -- forcing them through ErrorState's alert-role/red-icon treatment would fight that contract and require inventing a synthetic error object for something that isn't one. A new, small, genuinely reusable common component (no domain knowledge, just heading+optional message) was the cleaner fit and will likely be reused once frontend-ibkr-status-indicator (still planned) needs the same treatment.

decisions.decision: The category picker only exposes IBKR's own scan-type `code`/`display_name` (GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's `categories`, normalized via features/scanner/scannerCategories.ts's `toScannerCategories`). `scan_config`'s `instrument`/`location` fields are hardcoded to `'STK'`/`'STK.US.MAJOR'` (the exact defaults `IBKRScannerRunRequest.scan_config`'s own schema `examples` document) rather than exposed as further pickers.
decisions.rationale: GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's backend handler only ever forwards IBKR's `scan_type_list` -- it deliberately discards `instrument_list`/`location_tree` entirely (see backend-market-scanner's own decisions entry: 'passing through the raw scan_type_list... rather than hand-curating'), so there is no server-exposed option list this frontend could build an instrument/location picker from without inventing one client-side from scratch (duplicating gateway-versioned option data the backend explicitly chose not to model, for the same staleness-risk reason that task gave). Building a full instrument/location/filter-builder UI is also out of scope for this task's own 'pick a scan category, run it' framing (task description) -- that is a materially larger feature (a generic scan-config form) than what was asked for here. STK/STK.US.MAJOR was chosen over any other fixed pair specifically because it's the literal example the backend schema itself documents, not a value invented for this task.

decisions.decision: ScannerResultsTable imports and reuses features/watchlist/hooks/useAddWatchlistItem.ts directly for its per-row 'Add to watchlist' action, rather than writing a second POST /api/watchlist mutation hook under features/scanner/hooks/. This is the first cross-feature hook import in the codebase (every prior feature's hooks are only ever consumed from within that same feature's own components/pages).
decisions.rationale: useAddWatchlistItem already encapsulates the correct behavior end to end (idempotent no-op on a duplicate add per API.md, invalidates watchlist queries on success) -- duplicating it under features/scanner/hooks/ would risk the two implementations silently drifting (e.g. one gaining a bug fix or an invalidation the other doesn't). Frontend.md §3's placement rules explicitly restrict *component* placement (`components/common/` vs `features/<domain>/components/`, checked by pr-reviewer) but say nothing about restricting a mutation hook -- a thin wrapper over one `useMutation` call with no feature-specific rendering -- to only being called from within its own feature. Considered lifting `useAddWatchlistItem` (or the underlying `addWatchlistItem` API call) into a shared, feature-agnostic location instead; rejected since it already lives exactly where Frontend.md's hook-placement rule says a watchlist-domain hook belongs ('features/portfolio/hooks/usePortfolio.ts... lives under the feature it serves'), and moving it would only be justified if a third consumer made the watchlist feature itself feel like the wrong owner -- not yet the case here.

decisions.decision: common/ErrorState gained a fourth documented status case (429, alongside 404/422/503/0): a distinct 'Too many requests' heading/icon, plus a new `Try again in {retryAfterSeconds}s.` line rendered when `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` is non-null. Previously 429 fell through to the generic 'Something went wrong' default case, since no earlier frontend feature had ever called a rate-limited backend route (POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run is the first).
decisions.rationale: API.md documents 429 as a real, expected outcome of POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run (IBKRProvider's 1-request/second client-side throttle) and api/client.ts already parses the response's Retry-After header into `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` specifically so a caller doesn't have to -- leaving ErrorState's generic fallback in place for this endpoint's very first UI consumer would both mislabel a normal, actionable, retry-shortly outcome as 'Something went wrong' and leave that already-parsed retry delay unused. Rendering the retry delay as its own Typography line (not appended into `detail`'s string) was chosen so a future backend wording change to `detail` can never accidentally duplicate or contradict this app-owned line.

decisions.decision: Fixed the review's blocking finding by extracting a new `ScannerAddToWatchlistButton({ ticker })` component that calls `useAddWatchlistItem()` and owns its own `added` boolean state, and having ScannerResultsTable's action-column `render` return that component per row instead of a shared `useAddWatchlistItem()`/`addedTickers` Set at the table level. Added a regression test staggering two rows' POST /api/watchlist responses (MSFT resolving before AAPL despite AAPL being clicked first) proving both rows independently flip to 'Added'.
decisions.rationale: The bug was structural, not a state-tracking bug: TanStack Query's MutationObserver.mutate() detaches from whatever mutation it was previously observing as soon as a different mutate() call reattaches the same observer, so one useAddWatchlistItem() instance shared across rows could only ever track the most recently clicked row's onSuccess/isError. Reconciling addedTickers against some other source of truth (e.g. polling the watchlist query) was considered and rejected -- it would still leave a shared mutation's isPending/isError wired to only the latest click, and would add a second, redundant success-detection path instead of fixing the actual observer-sharing root cause. Giving each row its own hook call (one observer per row, matching how DataTable's render(row) already produces one React element per row) is the same pattern this codebase already uses for other per-row state and requires no changes to useAddWatchlistItem itself.

decisions.decision: Fixed round 2's first blocking finding by rewriting the regression test's two clicks to use synchronous `fireEvent.click()` (no `await` in between) instead of two sequential `await user.click()` calls. Verified the fix is real by checking out the pre-fix commit (61e9377) into a separate git worktree, copying the rewritten test file over unmodified, and running it there: the concurrency test now correctly fails against the old shared-mutation code (only 1 of 2 rows reaches 'Added') and passes against this branch's fix.
decisions.rationale: The reviewer proved `await user.click(a); await user.click(b)` never exercises genuine concurrency -- userEvent's returned promise doesn't resolve until React has flushed that click's own state updates, which given the mocked POST's short delay meant the first click's onSuccess had already fired before the second click was even dispatched. `Promise.all([user.click(a), user.click(b)])` was considered (also genuinely concurrent, since neither individual click promise is awaited before the second fires) but `fireEvent.click()` was chosen instead because it's what the reviewer's own comment named as the more direct fix, dispatches synchronously with no promise semantics to reason about at all, and needed no `userEvent.setup()` in this particular test now that no other user-event-only behavior (hover, typing) is exercised by it.

decisions.decision: Fixed round 2's second blocking finding by replacing ScannerAddToWatchlistButton's failed-add rendering of the full common/ErrorState block with a compact Tooltip-wrapped error IconButton (aria-label and Tooltip title both carry the failure's ApiError.detail; clicking it retries the same mutate() call). No existing 'compact inline error state for a table cell' component or convention was found anywhere in the codebase (grepped for Tooltip usage and every other per-row-mutation-error case -- PositionsTable.tsx, WatchlistTable.tsx -- both render ErrorState as a sibling above their whole table, never per-row/per-cell), so this is a new, narrowly-scoped pattern rather than a reuse of an existing one.
decisions.rationale: A full ErrorState block (icon + heading + body, meant to occupy a page/section) inside a <TableCell> makes that cell the tallest in its row and stretches every other cell in the same row to match, per the reviewer's finding. An icon-sized affordance keeps the row's height unchanged regardless of error state. A Tooltip (rather than inline Typography text, which would still add vertical space, just less of it) was chosen so the failure detail is available on demand (hover/focus) without permanently growing the cell at all; wrapping the retry action in the same control (rather than a separate icon plus a separate retry button) avoids adding a second interactive element to an already-narrow action column. Promoting this to a components/common/ component was considered and rejected for now -- with exactly one caller, extracting a common component ahead of a second real use case would be speculative generalization; if a second per-row-mutation-error case appears (e.g. frontend-position-risk-columns or a future per-row table action), that is the point to lift this into common/, not before.

decisions.decision: Resolved this task's `questions` entry via option (a) (an explicit round-4 dispatch instruction), fixing round 3's two blocking accessibility regressions without reworking `ScannerAddToWatchlistButton`'s Button/IconButton element swap itself: (1) a `useEffect` keyed on `addWatchlistItem.isError` calls `.focus()` on a `ref` attached to the retry `IconButton` the moment it mounts, restoring the keyboard focus the element swap otherwise drops to `document.body`; (2) an always-mounted, visually-hidden `Box` with `role="status"` (not `role="alert"`) sits alongside the button, its text content set to a `Failed to add {ticker} to watchlist: {detail}` string only while `isError` is true -- `role="status"`, not `role="alert"`, was chosen specifically so it doesn't reintroduce the 'full ErrorState alert-role landmark' this component's own round-3 regression test (`queryByRole('alert')).not.toBeInTheDocument()`) asserts is gone. Also rebased the branch onto current `main` in the same pass (58 commits behind at rebase time, not the 'hundreds' estimated at dispatch), resolving four real conflicts (`frontend/src/api/ibkr.ts`, `frontend/src/api/ibkr.test.ts`, `frontend/src/components/layout/NavDrawer.tsx`, `frontend/tests/mocks/handlers.ts`) by keeping both sides' additions, per the dispatch instructions.
decisions.rationale: Rewriting `ScannerAddToWatchlistButton` to keep one stable root DOM element across all three states (idle/pending/error) was considered as a more structural fix (avoiding the unmount/remount that caused the focus loss in the first place) but rejected for this round: the dispatch instructions specifically named the two-part fix (move focus programmatically; add a live-region announcement) as the accepted shape of the fix, and a full restructure changing the button's own element type across states risks introducing a third new regression in the same file the last two rounds already produced -- the narrower, additive fix is lower-risk given that history. An always-mounted live region (element persists, only its text mutates) was chosen over a mount-on-demand one (matching `common/ErrorState`'s own working `role="alert"` pattern) because it's the more robust pattern specifically for a `role="status"` (`aria-live="polite"`) region -- polite announcements are less reliably picked up on fresh DOM insertion than assertive (`alert`) ones are, unlike the `alert` case this component's own round-3 fix already proved works fine when mounted on demand.

comments.summary: Round 4 (re-review of commit 81116d2, the round-4 accessibility fix, plus a5f4a72's rebase of the branch onto current main). Both the focus-restoration effect and the always-mounted role="status" live region genuinely work for the transition they were built for: verified the focus test isn't tautological by deleting the useEffect and re-running ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx's 'moves focus to the retry control' test -- it fails without the fix (document.activeElement stays document.body) and passes with it; did the same for the live-region test by blanking failureAnnouncement's text, which likewise fails without the real implementation. Also spot-checked the 4-file rebase conflict resolution: frontend/src/api/ibkr.ts has both main's getIbkrStatus/recordIbkrBreadthSnapshot and this branch's getIbkrScannerParams/runIbkrScanner, each still imported and exercised by its own feature's hooks (useIbkrStatus.ts, useMarketBreadth.ts, useScannerParams.ts, useRunScanner.ts) and covered in ibkr.test.ts; NavDrawer.tsx has both 'Scanner' and 'Daily Homework' nav items, both routed in App.tsx (/scanner, /homework); tests/mocks/handlers.ts has both sides' MSW handlers with no duplicate registrations. Full suite otherwise clean: backend pytest 1239 passed/100% coverage, ruff+mypy clean; frontend vitest 878 passed, coverage 99.77%/99.07%/99.79%/99.82% (gate 90%), yarn lint + tsc -b --noEmit clean, profit-target wording guard clean; make e2e all 24 specs pass (still no scanner spec, already tracked on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups); no schema/route changes so openapi.json correctly untouched.

New blocking finding: the round-4 fix only restores focus for the isError false->true transition (the useEffect at line 71-75, keyed on addWatchlistItem.isError). It does nothing for the reverse isError true->false transition, which happens every single time a user clicks the retry IconButton -- calling mutate() immediately resets isError to false (synchronously, in the same dispatch that sets isPending true), which swaps the focused <IconButton> back out for a fresh <Button> in the same slot, dropping focus to document.body exactly the way the original round-3 bug did. If the retry then fails again, the effect happens to refire when isError flips back to true and masks the blip by refocusing the (new) retry icon -- but if the retry succeeds (the common case), isError never becomes true again, so focus is left on document.body permanently with nothing to reclaim it. I verified this two ways, not just by reading the code: (1) a throwaway RTL test asserting document.activeElement === document.body immediately after fireEvent-driven retry click, and again after that retry's success response resolves -- both true; (2) a real Chromium session (via Playwright, driving the actual Vite dev build with the scanner/watchlist network calls mocked at the browser level) reproducing the exact same golden-path-then-failure-then-successful-retry flow: after the successful retry, document.activeElement.tagName was 'BODY'. This is the same class of regression (an unmounted/remounted focused node) that round 3 introduced and round 4 was supposed to close out, just on the symmetric transition -- the task's own parked `questions` entry from round 2 flagged exactly this risk ('the per-row action-button component may benefit from being rethought as a whole... rather than incrementally patched a fourth time'), and this finding is that prediction playing out again.

Non-blocking design note (filed on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups): role="status" (aria-live="polite") for the failure announcement is a legitimate, working live region -- confirmed its text is set correctly and it's discoverable via getAllByRole('status') -- but WAI-ARIA authoring practice generally recommends role="alert" (assertive) for an action-failure announcement specifically because assertive announcements interrupt while polite ones can be skipped/queued behind other AT speech. The round-4 decisions entry chose status specifically to avoid conflicting with ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx's existing queryByRole('alert') assertion -- but that assertion was written to confirm the *full ErrorState block* (which broke row layout) was gone, not to forbid any use of role="alert" at all; a visually-hidden alert region would have no layout impact and wouldn't reintroduce what that test actually guards against. Not blocking since role="status" does function as a real, working live region, just a less assertive one than best practice suggests for an error case.

Second new blocking finding, from a parallel code-review pass (independently corroborated the focus-loss finding above, and additionally surfaced this): ScannerAddToWatchlistButton reuses features/watchlist/hooks/useAddWatchlistItem.ts (per this task's own cross-feature-hook-reuse decision), which uses a fixed, shared `mutationKey: watchlistKeys.add`. That same key drives WatchlistTable's `useMutationState({ filters: { mutationKey: watchlistKeys.add, status: 'pending' } })` (frontend/src/features/watchlist/components/WatchlistTable.tsx:85), which synthesizes a pending-add skeleton row -- and that hook's own doc comment explicitly assumes 'only one add mutation is ever in flight at a time in practice' (WatchlistTable.tsx:98), an assumption that predates this PR and this PR's own decisions entry doesn't revisit. Because a TanStack Query mutation lives in the single app-wide QueryClient's mutation cache regardless of which component/page dispatched it, a Scanner-page add that's still pending (useAddWatchlistItem's onSuccess awaits invalidateQueries, so the pending window spans the POST plus the refetch) bleeds into WatchlistTable the moment it's mounted -- e.g. the user clicks 'Add to watchlist' on /scanner, then navigates to /watchlist before that request settles. I independently reproduced this: a scratch RTL test mounting ScannerResultsTable and WatchlistTable under one shared QueryClient (matching the real app's single-QueryClientProvider setup), clicking a Scanner row's Add button, and confirming WatchlistTable renders a `data-testid="watchlist-skeleton"` row for a ticker the user never touched from the Watchlist page. This is a direct consequence of the cross-feature hook-reuse decision that wasn't caught in any prior round -- either give ScannerAddToWatchlistButton its own distinct mutationKey (e.g. via a thin scanner-owned wrapper around the same mutationFn) or scope WatchlistTable's useMutationState filter/assumption to account for a second caller.

Round 3 (re-review of commit b7c7f8b, which addresses both of round 2's blocking findings). Both round-2 fixes are verified correct: (1) copied the rewritten ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx unmodified into a separate git worktree checked out at the pre-fix commit (61e9377) and ran it there -- 2 of 6 tests failed, including 'resolves two concurrent adds on different rows independently (regression, PR #243)', confirming the fireEvent.click()-based rewrite genuinely exercises the race; the same test passes 6/6 on this branch. (2) The full-block ErrorState-inside-a-TableCell layout regression is gone -- confirmed via `expect(screen.queryByRole('alert')).not.toBeInTheDocument()` in the rewritten failure test, and the retry click genuinely re-fires the mutation and reaches 'Added'.

New blocking regression introduced by the round-3 fix itself: on a failed add, ScannerAddToWatchlistButton swaps from rendering a <Button> to rendering a completely different <IconButton> element in the same slot (the `if (addWatchlistItem.isError)` branch returns a different component tree, not an update to the existing one) -- React unmounts the old node and mounts a new one, so keyboard focus that was on 'Add to watchlist' when the request failed is dropped to document.body instead of moving to the new retry control. I verified this independently (not just the code-review sub-pass that first flagged it): wrote a throwaway RTL test that focuses the 'Add to watchlist' button, clicks it, waits for the retry icon to appear, and asserts `document.activeElement` -- confirmed `document.activeElement === document.body` (tagName 'BODY') after the error renders. This is strictly worse than both the pre-round-2 and round-2 behavior, where the same <Button> DOM node stayed mounted throughout (ErrorState was rendered as an added sibling, never replacing the button), so focus was never lost. A keyboard-only user who presses Enter on 'Add to watchlist' and gets a failure now has to tab from the top of the page to reach the retry control instead of just pressing Enter again.

Second new blocking regression from the same fix: replacing common/ErrorState (role="alert" -- confirmed at ErrorState.tsx:77, a live region assistive tech announces automatically) with a Tooltip+IconButton removes the only mechanism that proactively announced a failed add. The new aria-label/Tooltip title is only exposed when a user actually navigates to or hovers that specific element -- there is no live-region equivalent. A screen-reader user who clicks 'Add to watchlist' on one row and then moves on (e.g. to check another row) while the request is in flight gets no announcement at all when it fails, whereas the pre-round-3 ErrorState rendering would have been announced via its alert role regardless of where focus was. Needs either a live-region announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden aria-live region updated on failure) alongside the compact icon, or focus programmatically moved to the retry control on failure so at least a screen-reader user tracking that row's own control is caught up -- the current pattern satisfies neither.

Non-blocking nit: `ErrorOutlineIcon` is imported from `@mui/icons-material/ErrorOutlined` (line 3), which is MUI's `Error` icon in its 'Outlined' theme variant (byte-identical SVG path to `Error.js`) -- a filled solid-circle icon, not the lighter hollow-circle `ErrorOutline` family the local alias name implies (that would be `ErrorOutlineOutlined`). Purely cosmetic; still clearly reads as an error icon. Filed on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups.

Non-blocking nit: the retry `IconButton`'s `disabled={addWatchlistItem.isPending}` (inside the `isError` branch) is dead code -- TanStack Query's mutation reducer resets `error`/`isError` to `null`/`false` in the same synchronous dispatch that sets `isPending: true`, so `isError` and `isPending` are never both true and this prop can never actually take effect. Harmless, but worth cleaning up or replacing with a dedicated 'retrying' flag if disabling during retry was actually intended. Filed on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups.

review.notes:
Round 3 review. Both of round 2's blocking findings (fake-concurrency regression test, ErrorState-in-a-TableCell layout break) are correctly fixed and independently verified (isolated-worktree re-run of the pre-fix test, direct read-through of the new compact error component). However the fix to round 2's second finding introduced two new blocking accessibility regressions of its own (focus loss to document.body on a failed add; loss of common/ErrorState's role="alert" live-region announcement), both confirmed with a throwaway RTL test I wrote and ran myself rather than trusting a first pass's claim alone. This mirrors round 2's own shape (a correct fix for the named finding, but a new regression introduced in the same commit) -- I initially posted an 'accepted' PR review comment before a parallel code-review pass surfaced these two issues; that comment is superseded by this needs_work verdict and this task's review section (see the follow-up PR comment noting the correction). Full suite otherwise clean: backend pytest 1139 passed/99.95% coverage/ruff+mypy clean (no backend changes); frontend vitest 742 passed, coverage 99.73%/98.91%/99.73%/99.79%, yarn lint + tsc -b --noEmit clean, profit-target wording guard clean; make e2e all 18 specs pass (no scanner e2e spec yet, already tracked); scripts/validate_tasks.py clean; no API/schema changes so openapi.json correctly untouched. The two non-blocking icon-import/dead-prop nits are unchanged from before and remain filed on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups.

Round 4 review (PR #243, commit a7a284d; branch freshly rebased onto main at a5f4a72, 4 real conflicts spot-checked and confirmed correctly resolved -- both sides' functionality present, wired, and tested in ibkr.ts/ibkr.test.ts, NavDrawer.tsx+App.tsx routes, and tests/mocks/handlers.ts). The round-3 fix's two named regressions are genuinely fixed for the transition they target -- verified non-tautologically by deleting the useEffect (the focus test then fails) and blanking the live-region text (the announcement test then fails), each restored the test to green. But the fix is incomplete: it only handles the isError false->true transition. The symmetric isError true->false transition -- which fires on every retry click, since mutate() resets isError synchronously -- swaps the focused IconButton back out for a fresh Button with no focus restoration at all, reproducing the exact round-3 bug on the reverse edge. Confirmed with both a jsdom/RTL assertion and a real Chromium session driven via Playwright against the actual dev build (network mocked at the browser level): after a failed add followed by a successful retry, document.activeElement is document.body, permanently. This is a new blocking finding (see review.comments) rather than a full accept. Full suite: backend pytest 1239 passed/100% coverage, ruff+mypy clean; frontend vitest 878 passed, coverage 99.77%/99.07%/99.79%/99.82%, yarn lint + tsc -b --noEmit clean, profit-target wording guard clean; make e2e all 24 specs pass (still no scanner e2e spec, tracked); no schema/route changes, openapi.json correctly untouched. One non-blocking design note (role="status" vs role="alert" for the failure announcement) filed on frontend-market-scanner-page-followups alongside the pre-existing icon-import/dead-prop nits and missing-e2e-spec item.

questions.question: PR #243 has now hit 3 needs_work rounds, and each of the last two has shown the same shape: a correct, verified fix for the named finding that introduces a new regression in the same commit (round 2's fix broke row layout; round 3's fix to that broke keyboard focus + screen-reader announcement on a failed add). Per the orchestrator's 3-round retry cap, no further automatic fix round will be dispatched. Two ways forward: (a) authorize one more round with an explicit instruction to fix the focus-loss + lost live-region-announcement pair without introducing a new regression (e.g. keep the same DOM node across the success/pending/error states rather than swapping element types, and add a visually-hidden aria-live region or move focus to the retry control on failure), or (b) have a human review/patch ScannerAddToWatchlistButton directly given the repeated regression-on-fix pattern.
questions.context: Unlike the backend-trailing-profit-stop case (a single narrow, mechanical missing-filter bug), this PR's pattern -- two consecutive rounds each fixing what was asked but breaking something else in the same component -- suggests the per-row action-button component (ScannerAddToWatchlistButton) may benefit from being rethought as a whole (e.g. one component that keeps a stable root element across all its states) rather than incrementally patched a fourth time. Flagging for a decision rather than spending a 4th automated round on the same file.
